security_feature_bypassed: The secret-scrubbing chain that clears every DOE secret input when the part enters debug or scan mode or takes a fatal error. The OCP LOCK HEK seed fuse is declared with a register field type that carries no hardware clear, so it is outside that chain while all three of its sibling DOE secrets are inside it.
finding: src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_fuse_reg.rdl declares two field types for fuse storage: secret at :19, which carries hwclr, and Fuse at :21, which carries only sw/hw access, swwel and a cptra_pwrgood reset. fuse_hek_seed's field is declared Fuse at :147, while the two sibling DOE secret fuses are declared secret at :28 and :35. The consequence is visible in one always_comb in the block top: src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_top.sv:538, :542 and :550 each assign hwclr = clear_obf_secrets for the obf key, the UDS seed and the field entropy, and the HEK loop immediately after them at :557-559 only reads the value out. The omission is structural rather than a missed assignment, because the generated input struct for the Fuse type has a single member, swwel (src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_reg_pkg.sv:304-306), against four for the secret type (:289-294), so the block has no clear port to drive even deliberately. The generated field logic at src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_reg.sv:4066-4088 accordingly has no HW Clear branch while the same block implements six elsewhere, its only clear arm is the pwrgood reset at :4080-4082, and the stored value is returned unconditionally on the readback path at :7450. Directed simulation of one unmodified soc_ifc_reg confirms the behaviour: after programming all three families, asserting the scrubbing strobe clears the UDS seed and the field entropy while fuse_hek_seed still reads dec00000, it is unchanged after 50 further cycles with the strobe held, and a bus read at offset 0x3C0 returns it. A second, independent protection also excludes the seed: src/integration/rtl/caliptra_top.sv:999-1002 substitutes constants for four secrets on the path to their consumers while in debug or scan mode and src/libs/rtl/caliptra_macros.svh:19-22 defines the four matching constants, but the HEK seed is in neither, reaching the DOE raw at :1014 while its siblings arrive through the substituted _dbg signals at :1012-1013.
detection_method: Located by CSBC, an LLM-driven convergence method that reads the submitted tree on its own terms and looks for places where the design contradicts itself. Here the contradiction is internal and complete: the RDL defines a field type that carries a hardware clear and another that does not, three of the four DOE secret inputs are declared with the former and wired to the scrubbing strobe in one always_comb, and the fourth is declared with the latter and sits in the same always_comb with no clear at all. The candidate was then made falsifiable by measurement rather than by inspection: a structural audit computes the in-tree censuses without naming the audited signal, so a pattern that failed to match reports a wrong count instead of silently passing; a directed simulation of one unmodified soc_ifc_reg drives both families through the same bus on the same strobe; and a negative control gives the HEK family the sibling clear in a scratch copy and shows the identical bench flips. No external repository, no other revision of this design, and no expected-answer list was consulted at any point.
security_impact: The scrubbing strobe exists so that a party who obtains debug or scan visibility of the part finds no DOE key material resident. Three of the four DOE secret inputs honour it and the HEK seed does not, so exactly the transition that is supposed to make the part safe to inspect leaves the 256-bit obfuscated Hard Epoch Key seed in place. The readback path in this block is unconditional, so the survivor is recoverable by anything that can read the register, and the fuse's documented Caliptra-side access is read-only rather than no-access. The seed is also the DOE's source block for HEK derivation, so a resident value stays usable to drive that flow as well as to read out. A second, independent protection excludes it too: its three siblings are replaced by constants on the path to the DOE while in debug or scan mode, and the HEK seed is connected raw, so neither the storage clear nor the datapath substitution covers it. The exposure is bounded by cptra_pwrgood, which does clear the register, so this is a residue that persists for the remainder of the power cycle rather than permanently.
proposed_mitigation: In src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_fuse_reg.rdl:147, declare fuse_hek_seed's field with the secret type used by its siblings at :28 and :35 instead of the Fuse type at :21, so the field gains hwclr and the generated input struct gains the member to drive it.

Regenerate the register block and add the missing assignment in the same always_comb as its neighbours: in the foreach at src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_top.sv:557-559, drive soc_ifc_reg_hwif_in.fuse_hek_seed[i].seed.hwclr = clear_obf_secrets, matching :538, :542 and :550.

Close the second gap as well: add a debug-mode replacement constant alongside src/libs/rtl/caliptra_macros.svh:19-22 and substitute it for the HEK seed on the path to the DOE, so src/integration/rtl/caliptra_top.sv:1014 delivers a masked value in debug or scan mode as :1012-1013 already do for the siblings.

Add an assertion or a directed regression case that requires every DOE secret input register, including fuse_hek_seed, to read zero on the cycle after the scrubbing strobe asserts, so a future field-type change cannot silently reintroduce the omission.
exploit_or_attack_flow: A part in the field has its OCP LOCK HEK seed fuse programmed over the SOC-side interface, which src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_fuse_reg.rdl:146 records as SOC Access: RWL-S, so the 256-bit seed is resident in fuse_hek_seed at offset 0x3C0.

The part is put into a state that gives an outside party visibility of it: debug unlock, scan mode entry, or debug intent set. src/integration/rtl/caliptra_top.sv:997 raises cptra_in_debug_scan_mode on any of those.

That signal is folded into the secret-scrubbing strobe at src/integration/rtl/caliptra_top.sv:772 and delivered to the register block at :1466, which is the mechanism intended to remove all DOE key material before the part is inspected.
The strobe reaches the hardware clear of the obf key, the UDS seed and the field entropy (src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_top.sv:538, :542, :550) and those three registers go to zero.

It reaches no clear on the HEK family, because the field's type carries none (src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_fuse_reg.rdl:147 against :21) and the generated input struct has no such port (src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_reg_pkg.sv:304-306). The register keeps its programmed value; measurement shows it unchanged after 50 further cycles with the strobe held.

The party reads fuse_hek_seed back over the register interface, at 0x300303C0 in the software map (src/integration/rtl/caliptra_reg/caliptra_reg.h:11509). The readback path at src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_reg.sv:7450 is unconditional, so the eight dwords of the seed are returned.

The same residue also remains available to the DOE, which selects it as the source block for HEK derivation at src/doe/rtl/doe_fsm.sv:276, and it is not masked on the way there: src/integration/rtl/caliptra_top.sv:1014 connects it raw while :1012-1013 pass the siblings through debug-mode constant substitution.
The seed stays recoverable until a cptra_pwrgood cold reset, which does clear the register; the containment case in the directed simulation establishes that boundary.
